sections.content:
## What You'll Build

A complete personal portfolio website — live on the internet at your own GitHub Pages URL before this session ends. Not a template you filled out. Not a demo. A real website with your name, your bio, your projects, and your skills, built with Claude Code and deployed publicly.

This capstone uses: Claude Code, VS Code, Live Server, Git, GitHub Pages.

**By the end of this session you will have a URL you can send to people.**

**The Accomplishment Standard:** This capstone is complete when you can open a browser, type your GitHub Pages URL, and see your portfolio. Not when the code is written. Not when it looks good locally. When it's live. Set that as your goal before you start.

## Prerequisites

Before starting, confirm you have:
- Claude Code installed and authenticated (lesson 7-2)
- VS Code with Live Server extension (lesson 5-8)
- Git installed (lesson 5-12)
- A GitHub account (lesson 6-1)
- Your refined bio from lesson 3-7 (or write one now — 3 sentences about who you are and what you're learning)

sections.title: Personal Portfolio Website
sections.content:
## Step 1 — Create the Project Folder (5 min)

Open PowerShell and create a new folder for the portfolio:

```
mkdir C:\Users\YourName\Documents\portfolio
cd C:\Users\YourName\Documents\portfolio
```

Open this folder in VS Code:
```
code .
```

Then open the VS Code terminal (`Ctrl+\``) and launch Claude Code from the portfolio folder:
```
claude
```

---

## Step 2 — Brief Claude Code (10 min)

You get better results when you give Claude a complete brief rather than vague instructions. Paste this, filled in with your real details:

```
Build me a personal portfolio website. Here is everything about me:

Name: [your name]
Bio: [paste your refined bio from lesson 3-7, or write 3 sentences]
Background: [what you do or study, your city if comfortable]
Skills I'm learning: [list 5-8 AI tools from this course you've used]
A project I want to highlight: [describe one thing you've built — even if it's from this course]

Requirements:
- Modern, clean design — dark background with blue or indigo accents
- Single HTML file with inline CSS (no external frameworks or CDNs)
- Sections: Hero (name + tagline), About, Skills, Projects, Contact
- Fully responsive — works on mobile and desktop
- Fast to load — no JavaScript dependencies
- A 'Tools I Use' section listing AI tools from my learning
- Subtle animated gradient in the hero section
- Footer with GitHub link placeholder
```

Review what Claude Code proposes before accepting. If anything in the plan looks wrong, say so before it writes the files.

---

## Step 3 — Review and Refine in Browser (15 min)

**Open the site locally:**
1. Right-click `index.html` in VS Code Explorer
2. Select **Open with Live Server**
3. Your browser opens the portfolio

**Review it honestly.** Ask yourself:
- Does the hero section feel like me, or like a template?
- Is the color scheme something I'd actually choose?
- Are there any placeholder texts I need to fill in?
- Does it look right on a narrow window (mobile simulation)?

**Make specific change requests to Claude Code.** Not "make it better" — specific:
- "Change the accent color from blue to #6366F1 (indigo)"
- "Replace the placeholder project with this description: [your actual project]"
- "The about section feels too formal — rewrite it to match the tone of this text: [your bio]"
- "Add a second project card for my work on [something from this course]"

Run your `/review` custom command (from lesson 7-7) on the generated files to check for issues.

---

## Step 4 — Add Your Personal Touch (10 min)

Every portfolio built from the same prompt risks looking generic. Ask Claude Code:

```
Based on everything I've told you about myself, suggest one unique section
or design element that would make this portfolio feel specifically mine —
not something you'd add to a generic template.
```

Review the suggestion. If it resonates, implement it. If not, ask for a different idea. This is the difference between a portfolio that shows up in your browser and one you'd actually share.

---

## Step 5 — Deploy to GitHub Pages (10 min)

**Create the repository:**
1. Go to `github.com` and log in
2. Click **New repository**
3. Name it exactly: `yourusername.github.io` (replace `yourusername` with your actual GitHub username)
4. Set it to Public
5. Don't initialize with a README — leave it empty
6. Click **Create repository**

**Push your code:**

Back in the VS Code terminal (make sure you're in the `portfolio` folder):

```
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Launch portfolio — built with Claude Code"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/yourusername/yourusername.github.io.git
git push -u origin main
```

Replace `yourusername` with your actual GitHub username in both places.

**Enable GitHub Pages:**
1. Go to your repository on github.com
2. Settings → Pages
3. Under Source, select **Deploy from a branch**
4. Branch: `main`, folder: `/ (root)`
5. Click **Save**

**Wait 2–3 minutes**, then go to: `https://yourusername.github.io`

---

> **Note:** Wait another 2 minutes and refresh. GitHub Pages takes a few minutes to build on first deploy. If it still shows 404 after 5 minutes, check: Settings → Pages confirms the source is set to main branch; your repository is named exactly `yourusername.github.io` (lowercase).

---

## Step 6 — Share It (5 min)

Once the site is live:

1. Copy the URL: `https://yourusername.github.io`
2. Send it to someone — a friend, a colleague, anyone. This makes it real.
3. Add the URL to `notes/my-ai-dev-environment.md` under a new section: **Live Projects**
4. In Claude Code, ask: "Create a README.md for this repository that describes the portfolio and notes it was built with Claude Code"

You built a website. It's on the internet. You wrote zero lines from scratch.

---

## What to Do If You Get Stuck

**Problem: Claude Code produces broken HTML/CSS**
Ask Claude Code to open the browser console (right-click → Inspect → Console) and fix any errors it sees there.

**Problem: GitHub push fails with authentication error**
GitHub no longer accepts password authentication for pushes. You need a Personal Access Token: GitHub Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Generate new token (classic) → check `repo` scope. Use this token as your password when git prompts you.

**Problem: GitHub Pages deploys but shows an empty page**
Confirm your main file is named `index.html` (not `portfolio.html` or similar). GitHub Pages serves `index.html` from the root.

**Problem: Styles look wrong**
Open the browser's developer tools (F12), find the Elements panel, and look for any CSS errors. Ask Claude Code: "I'm seeing this issue in the browser: [describe it]. Please fix it."

sections.title: Workshop A — AI-Accelerated Portfolio Building
sections.content:
Use Claude Code to build your portfolio website 5x faster.

**Step 1 — Before writing any code**, ask Claude Code to help you design:
```
I'm building a portfolio website. Help me plan it:
1. What sections are essential for a [your role] portfolio?
2. What technologies should I use given my current skill level and goals?
3. What makes a portfolio stand out vs being generic?
4. What should I avoid that's common but ineffective?
```

**Step 2 — Generate the initial structure** with Claude Code:
"Create the complete file structure and initial HTML/CSS for a portfolio with: hero section, about, projects (with live demo and GitHub links), skills, and contact form."

**Step 3 — Iterate on the design** using AI: "The hero section feels generic. What are 3 alternative approaches that would make it more memorable for a [your role]?"

**Step 4 — Mandatory review:** After each major section is built, ask Claude Code: *"Review this section for both visual design quality and technical correctness. What would make it more professional?"*

sections.title: Workshop B — Portfolio Projects Section
sections.content:
Build a compelling projects section with AI assistance.

**Step 1 — List your top 3 real projects** to feature. For each, gather: what it does, the technology stack, any interesting technical challenges.

**Step 2 — Ask Claude Code** to write compelling project descriptions:
"Write project descriptions for my portfolio. For each project, craft: a 2-sentence hook that explains what it does and why it matters, then technical details. Tone: professional but accessible.

Project 1: [describe it]
Project 2: [describe it]
Project 3: [describe it]"

**Step 3 — Review and personalise** the descriptions — add anything uniquely true about your experience with the project that the AI couldn't know.

**Step 4 — Ask Claude Code to implement the project cards** with the written descriptions as content.

**Step 5 — Get peer feedback:** Show the projects section to one person. What is their first impression? What do they click first?

sections.title: Workshop C — Automated Portfolio Testing
sections.content:
Use Claude Code to write and run tests for your portfolio site.

**Step 1 — Ask Claude Code** to write automated tests for your portfolio:
```
Write automated tests for my portfolio website using Playwright.
Test:
1. All navigation links work (no 404s)
2. Contact form submits without errors
3. All images load correctly
4. Page loads in under 3 seconds
5. Mobile viewport looks correct (responsive check)
```

**Step 2 — Run the tests:**
```bash
npx playwright test
```

**Step 3 — Fix any failing tests.** Are these real issues in your portfolio?

**Step 4 — Add one more test** for something important to your portfolio (e.g., GitHub links are correct, project demos load).

**Step 5 — Run all tests after every major change** before deploying.

sections.title: Workshop D — Deploy and Iterate with AI
sections.content:
Deploy your portfolio and use AI to improve it based on feedback.

**Step 1 — Deploy the portfolio** to Vercel, Netlify, or GitHub Pages.

**Step 2 — Share with 3 people** in your target audience (potential employers, collaborators, clients). Ask for specific feedback:
- What's your first impression?
- Is anything unclear or missing?
- Would you click any of the project links? Why or why not?

**Step 3 — Compile the feedback** and share it with Claude Code:
"I received this feedback on my portfolio [paste feedback]. Prioritise the issues by impact and help me address the top 3."

**Step 4 — Implement the priority fixes** with Claude Code's help.

**Step 5 — Mandatory review:** Ask Claude Code: *"Review the updated portfolio against the original feedback. Did the changes address each concern? What feedback-driven improvements are still needed?"*

sections.title: Workshop E — Push Your Portfolio via GitHub MCP
sections.content:
In the main workshop you pushed using manual git commands. Here's the same task done entirely through Claude Code using GitHub MCP — no terminal, no git commands.

**When to use this approach:** Quick updates, automation, or when you want to manage GitHub without switching out of Claude.

**Step 1 — Make sure GitHub MCP is active** in your Claude Code session. If you haven't set it up, see lesson 8-8 for the config.

**Step 2 — Create (or verify) the repo via MCP:**
Ask Claude Code: "Using GitHub MCP, check if a public repository named 'yourusername.github.io' already exists under my account. If it doesn't, create it now."

**Step 3 — Push your portfolio files:**
Ask Claude Code: "Push my index.html to the main branch of yourusername.github.io. Commit message: 'Portfolio update via MCP'."

If you have multiple files (CSS, images), ask: "Push all files in this folder to the repo."

**Step 4 — Verify:**
Ask Claude Code: "Using GitHub MCP, read me the contents of index.html in my yourusername.github.io repository."

Claude should return the file contents — proof the push worked.

**Step 5 — Create a deployment issue:**
Ask Claude Code: "Create a GitHub issue in my yourusername.github.io repo titled 'Portfolio v1 live' with a body listing what's on the site: sections, tech used, and the live URL."

**Reflect:** You managed a GitHub repository — pushed files, verified content, created an issue — entirely from Claude's chat interface. This is the MCP workflow: Claude acts as your hands across every connected service.

sections.title: Workshop F — AI-Generated Auto-Deploy Pipeline for Your Portfolio
sections.content:
Add an AI-generated GitHub Actions pipeline to your portfolio so every future update deploys automatically and is validated before going live.

**Why this matters for a portfolio:** You'll be updating it over time — adding projects, updating your bio, refining the design. Without a pipeline, every update is a manual push with no safety check. With a pipeline, you push and the automation handles validation and deployment.

**Step 1 — Ask Claude Code to generate the pipeline:**
```
Generate a GitHub Actions workflow for my portfolio at yourusername.github.io.

The pipeline should:
1. Trigger on every push to main
2. Validate the HTML using htmlhint
3. Check index.html is under 500kb
4. Confirm the live site URL is responding (HTTP 200 check)
5. Output a summary: file size, validation result, and the live URL

Save to .github/workflows/deploy-check.yml
Explain what each section of the YAML does.
```

Read every line Claude generates. Ask about anything you don't understand.

**Step 2 — Push the workflow:**
Ask Claude Code: "Push .github/workflows/deploy-check.yml to my yourusername.github.io repository. Commit message: 'ci: add portfolio validation pipeline'."

**Step 3 — Trigger your first automated run:**
Make a small change to your portfolio — update the tagline or add a sentence. Ask Claude Code to push it. Then:
1. Go to github.com/yourusername/yourusername.github.io
2. Click the **Actions** tab
3. Watch your pipeline run step by step

**Step 4 — Make the pipeline fail on purpose:**
Ask Claude Code to temporarily add a broken HTML tag to index.html and push it. Does the pipeline catch it?

Fix the HTML, push again, confirm the pipeline passes.

**Step 5 — Add a lighthouse score step (optional):**
Ask Claude Code: "Can I add a Lighthouse performance audit to my GitHub Actions pipeline for free? If yes, add it and push the updated workflow."

This gives you automated performance scores on every deploy — the same tool Google uses to measure web performance.

**End state:** Your portfolio now has a full CI/CD pipeline. Every push triggers: HTML validation → size check → live URL check → (optionally) performance score. Broken code never goes live silently.

sections.question: You use Claude Code to build your portfolio and it produces 500 lines of CSS. You don't understand most of it but it looks correct. Is this acceptable?
options: Yes — the visual output is what matters
No — you should understand the code you publish; at minimum, ask Claude Code to explain the key CSS patterns and ensure no generated code has security implications
Yes — CSS is just styling and has no security implications
No — you must write all code yourself to put it in your portfolio
sections.explanation: Understanding the code you publish matters for several reasons: (1) you'll need to maintain and update it — if you don't understand it, every change requires AI assistance; (2) in interviews, you may be asked about your portfolio code; (3) it represents your capabilities. The correct approach: build with AI assistance, then ask Claude Code to explain each significant pattern so you understand the codebase you're presenting as your work.

sections.question: Your portfolio is complete but has no analytics. Why might you want analytics, and what is the most important metric to track?
options: No reason — portfolios don't need analytics
Analytics show you how potential employers/clients find and use your site — time on projects section and which projects they click tell you what's most effective
Analytics are only useful for e-commerce sites
You should track social media shares primarily
sections.explanation: Portfolio analytics help you optimise for your actual audience's behaviour. Key metrics: which projects get the most views (shows what interests your target audience), time spent on each section (shorter = less engaging, usually), where visitors come from (LinkedIn, GitHub, direct = how people are finding you), and bounce rate (are people leaving immediately?). This data lets you iterate based on evidence rather than guessing what makes an effective portfolio.

sections.content: **Capstone 14-1 complete.** You have a live portfolio website with an auto-deploy pipeline. Every tool you learned — Claude Code, VS Code, Git, GitHub MCP, GitHub Actions — came together in this single session. Your portfolio now validates and deploys automatically on every push. The next capstone builds a command-line research tool using the Anthropic API.
